skill.name: data-structure-protocol
skill.description: Give agents persistent structural memory of a codebase for dependency navigation, public API tracking, and impact analysis.
skill.summary: Map codebase structure into a persistent DSP graph for safer navigation and refactoring.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around prose, examples, and command names. The real risk is the unpinned remote download of dsp-cli.py and subsequent Python CLI execution in a workspace.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle dsp-cli.py with the skill, or require explicit user approval plus a pinned commit and checksum before download.
State that python dsp-cli.py commands should run only in trusted repositories after user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Command examples look executable by default
remediation.suggestion: Label examples as optional workflows and describe the files each command may read or modify.

content.value_statement: Large repositories are hard for AI agents to navigate without repeated orientation. This skill uses DSP metadata to map files, public APIs, imports, exports, and dependency reasons.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use a .dsp directory for codebase structure mapping.
Defines DSP graph concepts for objects, functions, imports, shared APIs, and exports.
Guides initial mapping from root entrypoints through reachable local imports.
Lists CLI workflows for creating, updating, deleting, navigating, searching, and diagnosing DSP entities.
Describes how to update DSP metadata when files, imports, exports, or purposes change.
Supports impact analysis by finding import recipients and explaining dependency reasons.
limitations: Requires Python 3.10+ and the dsp-cli.py helper script.
Only helps when DSP metadata exists or the user wants to create it.
Does not replace tests, code review, or environment-specific validation.
Records external dependencies as external objects, but does not analyze their internals.

use_cases.title: Understand a large repository
use_cases.description: Use DSP entries to find key modules, imports, exports, and dependency reasons before editing code.

use_cases.title: Plan a safe refactor
use_cases.description: Query parent and child relationships to identify affected files before moving APIs or replacing dependencies.

use_cases.title: Maintain structural memory
use_cases.description: Update .dsp metadata when files, public APIs, imports, or purposes change during development.

prompt_templates.title: Find project context
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner orientation in a DSP-tracked repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the DSP guidance to inspect this repository structure. Find the main entrypoints, important objects, and related public APIs before suggesting edits.

prompt_templates.title: Create initial DSP map
prompt_templates.scenario: Bootstrap DSP metadata for a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a DSP map for this project. Start from the root entrypoints, document reachable local imports, and record why each dependency exists.

prompt_templates.title: Update DSP after code changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Keep metadata aligned with a code modification.
prompt_templates.prompt: I changed files, imports, and public exports in this repository. Review the affected DSP entities and update descriptions, imports, shared APIs, and move records as needed.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze refactor impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Use DSP to analyze the impact of replacing this dependency. Find every recipient, explain why it imports the dependency, and propose a safe replacement sequence.

output_examples.input: Find what depends on the authentication service before I change it.
output: Identifies the DSP entity for the authentication service.
Lists direct and indirect recipients that import it.
Summarizes why each dependency exists and which public APIs may be affected.

output_examples.input: I added a new exported payment helper and one new import.
output: Creates or updates the relevant object and function entities.
Records the new shared API and import relationship.
Adds a short reason for the dependency so future impact analysis is useful.

output_examples.input: Map this repository from scratch with DSP.
output: Finds root entrypoints and documents reachable local files first.
Separates external dependencies from local code.
Builds a reviewable structure map in .dsp metadata.

best_practices: Update DSP immediately when creating files, changing imports, or changing public APIs.
Write short dependency reasons that explain why each import exists.
Review .dsp diffs with the same care as source code changes.
anti_patterns: Do not update DSP for internal implementation changes that do not affect purpose or dependencies.
Do not replace stable UIDs when a file is renamed or moved.
Do not model every local variable or private helper as a DSP entity.

faq.question: What is DSP?
faq.answer: DSP is a plain-text graph that records code entities, imports, exports, and reasons for dependencies.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when a repository has .dsp metadata or when you want to create and maintain that metadata.

faq.question: Does this replace normal documentation?
faq.answer: No. It is structural memory for agents, not complete human-facing project documentation.

faq.question: Does it analyze third-party packages?
faq.answer: No. Third-party packages are recorded as external dependencies, but their internals are not analyzed.

faq.question: What files does DSP create?
faq.answer: It stores small plain-text files under .dsp for entities, descriptions, imports, shared APIs, and reverse indexes.

faq.question: What should I verify before running commands?
faq.answer: Confirm the dsp-cli.py source, review any download instructions, and run commands only in trusted repositories.
